units.title: Combine two groups
units.introduction: Combining a group of 2 with a group of 3 makes 5. You can count on from the first group.
units.prompt: A tray has 4 cups. You add 3 more. How many cups are there?

rubric.full_credit: Produces 7, by counting on or any valid addition method.
rubric.partial_credit: Identify the right approach but make one local slip; verify on a fresh item before independent success.

units.title: Combine equal-sized parts
units.prompt: What is 1/2 + 1/3? Show the equally sized parts you used.

rubric.full_credit: Converts to 3/6 + 2/6 and obtains 5/6; accepts equivalent exact fractions with a valid method.
rubric.partial_credit: Identify the right approach but make one local slip; verify on a fresh item before independent success.

verification.method: Fraction arithmetic plus independent common-denominator calculation

units.title: Recognize even integers
units.outcome: Classify integers divisible by 2, including zero and negatives.
units.introduction: An integer is even if it equals 2 times an integer. For example, 6 = 2 × 3; 5 cannot be written this way with an integer.
units.prompt: Which of -4, 0 and 3 are even? Give an integer multiplier for each one you select.

rubric.full_credit: Selects exactly -4 and 0, with multipliers -2 and 0.
rubric.partial_credit: Identify the right approach but make one local slip; verify on a fresh item before independent success.

verification.method: Integer divisibility and reconstruction by multiplication

units.title: Trace two statements
units.outcome: Predict the order of output from consecutive print calls.
units.introduction: print displays its argument. Consecutive statements run in order: print("A") then print("B") displays A on one line and B on the next.
units.prompt:
What does this display?

print("start")
print("finish")

rubric.full_credit: Gives start then finish on separate lines.
rubric.partial_credit: Identify the right approach but make one local slip; verify on a fresh item before independent success.

verification.method: Executed with an isolated Python process and independently traced statements

units.title: Find a function body and call
units.outcome: Distinguish a function definition, its body, and a call.
units.introduction: def names a function; its indented statements are the body. Defining it does not run its body. A later name() call runs it.
units.prompt:
In this snippet, which line defines the function, which line is its body, and which line calls it?

def greet():
    print("hello")
greet()
units.key: Definition: def greet():; body: print("hello"); call: greet()

rubric.full_credit: Identifies all three parts and their relationships; no requirement to predict output.
rubric.partial_credit: Identify the right approach but make one local slip; verify on a fresh item before independent success.

verification.method: Parsed syntax tree plus executed definition-only and definition-with-call variants
